# Station data-quality audit (RQ1)

*Generated by `python -m src.clean.audit_report` from pipeline outputs. Do not edit by hand. Blinding: nothing in this report compares NCAP with non-NCAP cities.*

## 1. What was audited

565 CPCB continuous stations (CAAQMS), 2015-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (Indian dates). 15-minute PM2.5 and PM10 from the CPCB mirror to the end of 2025 and from OpenAQ for January-March 2026, on the corrected clock (DEC-054). Stations with any PM data by year of first data:

| first_year | stations |
|---|---|
| 2015 | 30 |
| 2016 | 18 |
| 2017 | 42 |
| 2018 | 49 |
| 2019 | 66 |
| 2020 | 56 |
| 2021 | 66 |
| 2022 | 75 |
| 2023 | 127 |
| 2024 | 22 |
| 2025 | 14 |

## 2. Is the source trustworthy?

The mirror was checked against OpenAQ's independent copy of the same CPCB data at every overlapping station-year (`docs/mirror-openaq-crosscheck.md`). 2019-2021 values are identical; IMD-operated stations differ at 15 minutes but agree on daily means; OpenAQ's March 2018 PM2.5 is an index, not a concentration (DEC-057). Station coordinates were settled from identical values (`docs/station_metadata_review.md`, DEC-058, DEC-059, DEC-067): station 513, urban_centre 27, station_unconfirmed 20, locality 3, none 2; 5 stations await a decision.

## 3. Impossible values and instrument ceilings (15-minute values)

Values at or below zero: 100,998 15-minute values, all in 2026, i.e. in the OpenAQ data used for January-March 2026. The mirror holds none. The mirror is CPCB's validated data, OpenAQ the raw feed: in 2025, where both exist, OpenAQ has 2.6% of PM2.5 values at or below zero and the mirror is empty at 100.0% of those slots; OpenAQ has PM2.5 > PM10 in 1.43% of slots, the mirror in 0.04% (`docs/mirror-openaq-crosscheck.md` §6, DEC-079). So January-March 2026 is at a lower validation level than 2015-2025: the flags here remove the impossible and PM2.5 > PM10 values, but not whatever else CPCB's validation removes. Instrument ceilings are found from the network-wide histogram (DEC-068): a value that is more than 10 times as frequent as values of the same precision within ±10 µg/m³, at 5+ stations. ## 5. Level shifts (changepoints)

PELT on each station's weekly departure from its neighbours' median (or its own deseasonalised series where it has no two neighbours within 25 km), segments of at least 26 weeks, penalty calibrated so that at most 5% of block-shuffled (no-shift) series show a changepoint (DEC-078), steps of at least 25% (DEC-072). A step can be a recalibration, an instrument change or a move, or a real local change beside the monitor; the audit cannot tell which.

Penalty calibration (`null_false_alarm` = share of shuffled series with a spurious changepoint; `real_share_with_shift` = share of real series with one):

| penalty | null_false_alarm | real_share_with_shift | series | reference | chosen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.180 | 0.686 | 582 | neighbours | False |
| 5 | 0.061 | 0.552 | 582 | neighbours | False |
| 8 | 0.027 | 0.399 | 582 | neighbours | True |

## 11. Satellite units and the oversized-polygon rule

1923 units enter the primary satellite layer; 10 buffered NCAP towns without a GHSL centre enter only a sensitivity analysis (DEC-063). The primary city value is the population-weighted mean over the polygon for every unit; the area-weighted mean is the sensitivity check (DEC-070). How much the choice matters (ACAG V5.GL.06, 2015-2024, % difference population- vs area-weighted):

| units | median_diff_pct | p95_abs_diff_pct | median_within_unit_sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| all | 0.21 | 1.25 | 0.58 |
| over 1,000 km² | 1.72 | 3.72 | 2.38 |

## 12. Limits of this audit

- A level shift cannot be told apart from a real local change next to a monitor.
- Stations without two neighbours (isolated) get no neighbour check; their changepoints use their own seasonal cycle and can reflect regional change.
- The satellite check is only as independent as ACAG is of the ground network (it is calibrated to it).
- 27 stations keep an approximate city point; they are used for city assignment, not neighbour checks.
